sections.h2: Why Lansing sellers record deeds in Mason
sections.html:
Mason holds the county seat, even though most of Lansing, the state capital, sits inside Ingham County. The recording desk is the Register of Deeds, 2nd Floor, 341 S. Jefferson Street, Mason, MI 48854. Mail goes to PO Box 195 at the same town, and the phone is 517-676-7216.

The front counter is staffed weekdays from 8 until 5. Older books live in the vault, which is open 8:30 to 4 by appointment only. A seller coming from East Lansing or Okemos should phone before making the drive.

The county fee schedule sets $30.00 for any deed, mortgage, lis pendens, certified court paper or similar real estate instrument, however many pages it runs. Smaller charges stack up when several papers file on the same day.

Ingham County recording and copy charges
ServiceCharge
Record a deed, mortgage or similar instrument$30.00
Each liber and page or instrument number named in a multi-instrument assignment or discharge$3.00
Time-stamped copy, only when the original is submitted50 cents a page
Copy of a recorded document$1.00 a page
Certified copy of a whole recorded document$5.00 plus $1.00 a page
Treasurer's tax certificate, up to five parcel numbers$5.00

Payment is expected at recording, following MCL 600.2567.

sections.h2: Does the Treasurer have to sign off before a warranty deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Yes. A tax certificate from the County Treasurer is a precondition for recording a warranty deed, covenant deed, land contract, or an assignment of land contract that carries a warranty clause. The same gate covers an affidavit fixing the legal description in one of those papers, and condominium master deeds, amendments that alter the legal description included.

The certificate is $5.00 for five parcel numbers and $0.20 for each one after that, citing MCL 211.135. A seller with a split or multi-parcel property should count the tax IDs first. Treasurer telephone: 517-676-7220. Ask for the certificate before the closing date, so it is already in hand when the title company sends the deed to Mason for recording.

sections.h2: Transfer tax: who pays and how much
sections.html:
The county's fee page puts the burden on the seller or grantor, payable when the instrument arrives for recording. The rates are $3.75 per $500 (state) and $0.55 per $500 (county). Divide the price by $500, round any fraction up to the next block, and multiply by the combined rate. The deed shows total consideration on its face, or a Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit comes with it, and any claimed exemption has to be written on the instrument.

The county tax falls under MCL 207.501 through 207.513 and the state tax under MCL 207.521 through 207.537. Three odd cases come up:

  • Land spanning two counties needs the price divided by parcel, and each county taxes its piece.
  • County tax applies to the price named in a foreclosure instrument.
  • A deed of easement or right of way is taxable as well.

Exemptions sit in MCL 207.505 and MCL 207.526.

sections.h2: What the Mason office checks on a deed
sections.html:
The office's recording requirements list covers only the common problems, but it is a useful pre-flight check:

  • Original ink signatures, typed or printed names beneath, black or dark blue.
  • An acknowledgment with the notary's signature, county and state of commission, expiration date and the place of signing.
  • A certified death certificate recorded as a separate document and cross-referenced when a survivor is named.
  • Court orders certified under the clerk's raised seal.
  • No correction fluid or tape.
  • A top margin of 2.5 inches on page one, and Social Security numbers cut to four digits or fewer.

The underlying rules are in Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, and neighboring sections.

sections.h2: How far back the online records reach
sections.html: The index goes to 1956, and images start in 1960. Choose among three tools: Direct Search, a free index lookup that leaves out the latest seven days; Tapestry, at $8.95 a search with $1.00 per printed page; and Laredo, a subscription aimed at regular title searchers. For the years 1956 to 1981, check the vault by appointment, since county staff are still auditing indexed data from that stretch. Laredo subscription questions go to 517-676-7294. Pre-1960 copies are $1.00 a page at the Mason office or by mail to Register of Deeds Copies, P.O. Box 195, Mason, MI 48854.

sections.h2: Which other offices an Ingham County seller phones
sections.html:
The county home page publishes direct lines for the offices a sale tends to touch. Gather paperwork from them ahead of the closing date.

  • Treasurer, 517-676-7220: tax certificates and parcel tax status.
  • Register of Deeds, 517-676-7216: recording, copies, vault appointments.
  • Probate Court, 517-483-6300: estates, when an owner has died and the house passes through probate.
  • County Clerk, 517-676-7201: listed beside the Register of Deeds among the county's elected officials.
  • 30th Judicial Circuit Court, 517-483-6500: judgments and orders that may need recording against the property.

The courthouse is at 341 S. Jefferson, Mason, MI 48854, and the county also has an Equalization office for valuation questions.

If the parcel has an unpaid balance, ask the Treasurer at 517-676-7220 for the amount before you list. The title company will pay it from your proceeds at closing, and the tax certificate for a warranty deed cannot be issued until the parcel's tax standing is settled. Sellers who want a quick sale without repairs or lender delays sometimes go the cash route, but the recording steps stay the same: certificate, transfer tax, and the $30.00 filing. Bring or send the original signed deed, and ask the title company which of you will deliver it so nothing is filed twice. If you are coming in person, phone 517-676-7216 first to confirm the counter is staffed and that the deed meets the format list above. A rejected deed means a second trip to Mason and a delayed closing, which is easy to avoid with a quick call.

Ingham County is home to Lansing, East Lansing, Mason and Michigan State University. The 2025 estimate is 289,709 people, with 59.5 percent of homes owner-occupied. A typical home is valued at $198,800 and typical rent is $1,084.

faqs.q: When is the Ingham County recording counter open?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The vault closes earlier, with appointment hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Call 517-676-7216 to book.

faqs.q: Who writes the check for transfer tax in Ingham County?
faqs.a: The seller or grantor, as the county fee page describes it. Payment comes due as the deed is presented, at $3.75 per $500 for the state and $0.55 per $500 for the county.

faqs.q: Must I visit the Treasurer before my Ingham County deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Only for warranty deeds, covenant deeds and land contracts, which need a tax certificate first. It costs $5.00 for up to five parcel numbers and $0.20 for each extra one.

faqs.q: Is there a free way to search Ingham County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes, Direct Search is free and covers the index from 1956 forward, minus the most recent seven days. Seeing images through Tapestry costs $8.95 a search, and printing adds $1.00 a page.

faqs.q: Is the Ingham County Register of Deeds located in Lansing?
faqs.a: No. The office is in Mason at 341 S. Jefferson Street, 2nd Floor, because Mason is the county seat although Lansing lies mostly within the county.
